column2: Software Development using AI
UG

This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes. The curriculum addresses Model Context Protocol and developer tools, iterative human-agent coding loops and failure analysis, automated testing and code reliability evaluation using JUnit, and specification-driven development with context engineering. Target students are upper-level undergraduate students in the BTech Computer Science and Engineering programme who possess strong programming and software development fundamentals. Through lectures, tutorials, and practical laboratory sessions involving hands-on coding and project work, students learn to configure agentic workflows, analyze failure modes, evaluate code correctness, and justify context engineering strategies for complex software features.

Course Code: Configure an agentic software development workflow using Model Context Protocol (MCP) and tool integrations, given a set of software requirements and a list of available developer tools, such that the configured agent successfully executes at least 80% of the specified tool calls without human intervention.
column2: Analyze the performance and failure modes of an iterative human-agent coding loop, for a multi-file software modification task using a provided agent orchestration framework, identifying at least three distinct failure causes with supporting log evidence.
column3: Evaluate the reliability and correctness of code generated by an AI coding agent, using automated test suites and evaluation frameworks built on top of JUnit, justifying each evaluation verdict against a predefined test coverage and functional correctness specification.
column4: Justify context engineering strategies and specification-driven development plans, for a complex software feature request given a legacy codebase, covering every use case in the supplied requirements document.
